To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the individual determinants of research use in nursing practice are underdeveloped.
the individual determinants of research utilizations were not well represented by the models tested in this study.

the individual determinants of research use in this sample are a positive attitude toward nursing research, belief suspension (a measure of the extent to which nurses are willing to suspend their beliefs about a particular problem or issue in order to try out a different solution), and the number of in-services attended.
In summary, our research is concerned with

how nurses’ attitudes toward research, belief in the value of research, belief suspension in the face of contradictory evidence, and the amount of in-services attended influence the extent to which nurses use research in clinical practice.
the use of research in nursing practice.
the use of research by nurses in clinical practice.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the individual determinants of research use are not well understood.

the individual factors that have been identified in the literature as potentially influencing nurses’ research utilization do not appear to exert direct effects on research utilization when controlling for the other factors.
the individual-level factors that were tested in this study were not found to be strong predictors of research utilization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are not ready yet to model research utilization.
research utilization is a complex phenomenon and that we have only just begun to understand its determinants.
the individual factors that have been identified as determinants of research use have only a modest effect on research use, and the effects are inconsistent.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to develop a better understanding of the factors that influence nurses to use research in practice.
we have to do more to develop our descriptive knowledge about the determinants of nurses’ use of research.
we have a long way to go before we have a well-developed model of the individual determinants of research use.
